chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Kuleyb Al-Asady, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifice (al-nahr), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for Mina, then it is three days, and as for in the cities (al-buldan), then it is one day.'
ai.seo_question: What are the days for animal sacrifice during Hajj in Mina versus other cities?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the temporal scope of the sacrificial rite (nahr) by distinguishing between the extended period in Mina and the single day in other regions, reflecting the jurisprudential consensus on the days of Tashriq. It underscores the flexibility granted to pilgrims in Mina while maintaining the strictness of the main sacrifice day elsewhere, a distinction crucial for understanding the practical application of Hajj rituals in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Kuleyb Al Asady who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sacrifice, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for Mina, so it is three days, and as for in the (other) cities, so it is one day’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Kulayb al-Asadiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is three days in Mina’, but in the cities, it is only one Day.”
